newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Friday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.93/2.88 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 2.96/2.91 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.73/2.68 percent against 2.75/2.70 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from Thursday's close of S$98.53/98.58 and May 2002 unchanged at S$99.33/99.38.
June 2003 ended at S$94.34/94.44 versus Thursday's close of S$94.33/94.38.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent against Thursday's 3-5/16 3-3/16 percent.
